say: Why don't I see Nibbana right now?

note: listener tries to answer first - this pause IS the learning

say: You don't see Nirvana right now because you are seeing what you see because you are looking, and you don't know it. Like a dog halfway across a stream on a plank, wagging its tail at its own image in the water: it imagines another dog there, a 'water-dog'. It thinks it is looking because there is something out there to be seen. The moment it realizes it is seeing because it is looking, it stops looking.

text:
The basic principle underlying this whirlpool is to be found in our
bodies. What we call 'breathing' is a continuous process of emptying and
filling up. So even the so-called 'life-principle' is not much different
from the activity of a whirlpool. The functioning of the lungs and the
heart is based on the same principle and the blood circulation is in fact
a whirling round.

text: Where the winding ends and the rewinding begins is a matter beyond our comprehension. But one thing is clear all these comes to cease when craving and grasping are abandoned.

say: Where the winding ends and the rewinding begins is a matter beyond our comprehension. But one thing is clear all these comes to cease when craving and holding on are abandoned.

text:
The world arises in the six sense-bases. It is at the same time the
arising of suffering... The law of dependent arising is an explanation
of the way a concept of the world comes about. This is an extremely
subtle point.

text:
The deepest point of the entire formula of paticca samuppada is
traceable to the interrelation that obtains between name and form on
the one hand, and between name-and-form and consciousness on the other.

say: The deepest point of the entire formula of paticca samuppada — nothing happens on its own — is traceable to the interrelation that obtains between name and form on the one hand, and between name-and-form and consciousness on the other.

text:
Like an expert physician, who treats the germ of a disease and
immunizes the patient, the Buddha effected a breach in the saṃsāric
vortex by concentrating on its epicycle within this fathom-long body.

text:
All the twelve links are dependently arisen, and avijjā is no
exception. Even ignorance arises with the arising of influxes,
āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayo. So even ignorance is not the cause. The
cause is the underlying principle itself.

say: All the twelve links are dependently arisen, and avijja — not seeing how it works — is no exception. Even not seeing how it works arises with the arising of influxes, asavasamudaya avijjasamudayo. So even not seeing how it works is not the cause. The cause is the underlying principle itself.

text:
What is called the cessation of consciousness has a deeper sense here.
It means the cessation of the specifically prepared consciousness,
abhisaikhata vinnana. An arahant's experience of the cessation of
consciousness is at the same time the experience of the cessation of
name-and-form.

say: What is called the stopping of consciousness has a deeper sense here. It means the stopping of the specifically prepared consciousness, abhisaikhata vinnana — just knowing, before words. An arahant's experience of the stopping of consciousness is at the same time the experience of the stopping of name-and-form.

text:
True to the qualities of the Dhamma — to be seen here and now, not
involving time, and inviting to come and see — the entire mass of samsaric
suffering ceases immediately.

text:
According to the accepted interpretation, presented by the venerable
author of the Visuddhimagga, the first two links of the formula belong to
the past, and the last two links belong to the future. The remaining
eight links in the middle are taken to represent the present. That means,
we have here the three periods of time. So it is not — timeless.

say: According to the accepted interpretation, presented by the venerable author of the Visuddhimagga, the first two links of the formula belong to the past, and the last two links belong to the future. The remaining eight links in the middle are taken to represent the present. That means, we have here the three periods of time. So it is not — timeless.

text:
In order to ascertain whether a banana trunk is pith-less, it is not
necessary to go on removing its bark, layer after layer, from top to
bottom. We only have to take a sharp sword and cut the trunk in the
middle, so that the cross-section will reveal to us its pith-less nature.
Similarly, if we cut in the middle the banana trunk of preparations with
the sharp sword of wisdom, its internal structure as revealed by the
cross-section will convince us of the essence-less nature of the group
of preparations.

say: In order to ascertain whether a banana trunk is pith-less, it is not necessary to go on removing its bark, layer after layer, from top to bottom. We only have to take a sharp sword and cut the trunk in the middle, so that the cross-section will reveal to us its pith-less nature. Similarly, if we cut in the middle the banana trunk of things the mind makes with the sharp sword of wisdom, its internal structure as revealed by the cross-section will convince us of the essence-less nature of the group of things the mind makes.

text:
To the one attached, there is wavering. To the
unattached one, there is no wavering. When there is no wavering, there
is calm. When there is calm, there is no inclination. When there is no
inclination, there is no coming and going. When there is no coming and
going, there is no death and birth. When there is no death and birth,
there is neither a 'here' nor a 'there' nor a 'between the two'. This
itself is the end of suffering.

say: To the one attached, there is wavering. To the unattached one, there is no wavering. When there is no wavering, there is calm. When there is calm, there is no inclination. When there is no inclination, there is no coming and going. When there is no coming and going, there is no death and birth. When there is no death and birth, there is neither a 'here' nor a 'there' nor a 'between the two'. This itself is the end of suffering.
